meta.attribution: Ownership facts come from the company's own site, from the private equity or public-market filing that names its owner, or from an FTC enforcement record where one exists. Where a company's own consumer-facing site does not name its owner, the note says so and that absence is itself part of the transparency score, not a gap in this research. Location counts come from a company's own site, its own press release, or established veterinary trade press describing a specific transaction or report, and are dated to the source; a chain's true current count may have moved since. Reviewed 2026. Suggest corrections through Contribute.

criteria.label: Locations and ease of getting an appointment
How clearly it discloses who owns it

products.name: Banfield Pet Hospital
products.description: A general-practice chain built inside and near PetSmart stores, the largest single veterinary network in the US.

accessibility.note: Banfield's own site says it operates 'more than 1,000 hospitals in neighborhoods across the country and Puerto Rico,' most of them built inside or next to PetSmart stores.

ownership.note: Banfield's own site says it 'joined the Mars, Incorporated family of businesses' in 2007 and identifies itself as 'an Affiliate of Mars, Incorporated.' Mars is a privately held, family-owned conglomerate that does not file public financial reports the way a stock-market company must.

transparency.note: Banfield names its owner directly on its own consumer-facing about page, stating the Mars relationship and the year it began, rather than describing itself only in general terms.

products.name: VCA Animal Hospitals
products.description: A standalone general, specialty, and emergency hospital network, bought by Mars in 2017.

accessibility.note: Trade publication Today's Veterinary Business reported that Mars completed its acquisition of VCA Inc., which 'operates more than 800 veterinary hospitals across the United States and Canada,' in September 2017.

ownership.note: Today's Veterinary Business reported the deal closed at '$9.1 billion' and '$93 per share,' with Mars completing the acquisition on September 12, 2017. Mars is a privately held conglomerate and does not file the public financial reports a listed company must.

transparency.note: VCA's own about-us page states plainly that 'VCA joined the Mars family in 2017,' naming its owner directly rather than describing itself only as independent or hometown.

products.name: National Veterinary Associates
products.description: A general-practice, equine, and pet-resort chain that operates mostly under local practice names rather than one national brand.

accessibility.note: AVMA's own news coverage of NVA's 2023 restructuring says NVA operates 'more than 1,500 freestanding veterinary hospitals and pet resorts.'

ownership.note: NVA is owned by JAB Holding Co. AVMA's coverage confirms JAB acquired NVA in 2019. The FTC's February 2020 order found that JAB's combined ownership of Compassion-First Pet Hospitals and NVA would violate antitrust law in three local markets and required divestiture of three clinics; FTC Chair Lina Khan's June 2022 statement on a related JAB deal calls JAB 'a repeat offender' and describes the risk of private equity 'stealth roll-ups' that can 'strip productive capacity, degrade the quality of goods and services, and hinder competition.'

products.name: Ethos Veterinary Health
products.description: A specialty and emergency hospital network split off from NVA in 2023, also owned by JAB Holding.

accessibility.note: AVMA's news coverage of the 2023 NVA restructuring says Ethos Veterinary Health manages '145 specialty veterinary hospitals,' a narrower, referral-based network compared with general practice chains.

ownership.note: The FTC's June 2022 statement from Chair Lina Khan describes this as the second Commission consent order against JAB over its veterinary roll-up, after JAB's proposed acquisition of SAGE Veterinary Partners would have combined with its existing Compassion-First and NVA holdings to control 'nearly 100 specialty and emergency clinics'; the FTC ordered divestiture of clinics in Richmond, Va., Denver, San Francisco, and the Washington, D.C. area and imposed a 10-year prior-approval requirement on future JAB veterinary purchases near its existing clinics.

products.name: Thrive Pet Healthcare
products.description: A general-practice, specialty, and emergency chain backed by a private equity firm, formerly known as Pathway Vet Alliance.

accessibility.note: TSG Consumer Partners' own portfolio page says Thrive operates '~340 general practice, specialty, and emergency veterinary hospitals' plus '~115 veterinary clinics' across the US.

ownership.note: TSG Consumer Partners' own site lists Thrive Pet Healthcare among the brands it invests in, describing itself as able to make 'minority or majority investments' but not stating its exact stake in Thrive.

transparency.note: Thrive's own consumer-facing site does not name TSG Consumer Partners or any parent company anywhere on its homepage; it describes itself only as 'backed by a community of veterinary experts across the nation.'

products.name: Mission Pet Health
products.description: A general-practice chain formed by the 2024 merger of Mission Veterinary Partners and Southern Veterinary Partners.

ownership.note: Shore Capital Partners' own portfolio page says 'Mission Pet Health is one of the leading veterinary care organizations in the U.S., formed by the merger of Southern Veterinary Partners and Mission Veterinary Partners,' and lists Shore Capital Partners as its investor since December 2024.

products.name: AmeriVet Veterinary Partners
products.description: A general-practice chain backed by a private equity firm, growing mainly by buying existing independent practices.

accessibility.note: Investment bank Houlihan Lokey's own announcement of a November 2023 financing for AmeriVet describes it as 'a leading veterinary services platform with more than 200 clinics across 35 states.'

ownership.note: AEA Investors' own press release announcing its February 25, 2022, acquisition describes AmeriVet as 'a leading veterinary services platform with approximately 140 animal hospitals across more than 30 states' at the time, bought by AEA's Middle Market Private Equity team together with an unnamed 'LP Co-Investor.'

transparency.note: AmeriVet's own about-us page does not name AEA Investors, or any other owner or investor, anywhere on the page; it describes company growth only in general terms.

products.name: Vetco Total Care
products.description: Full-service veterinary hospitals built inside Petco pet care centers, run by the publicly traded Petco Health and Wellness Company.

accessibility.note: Petco's own press release on buying out Thrive Pet Healthcare's stake in their joint venture says Petco operated 'nearly 100 full-service veterinary hospitals' at that point, all inside Petco stores; the network has continued opening locations since.

ownership.note: The same press release identifies Petco as 'publicly traded on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol WOOF,' meaning it answers to public shareholders and must file regular reports with the SEC, unlike a privately held chain.

transparency.note: Petco's own corporate site describes Vetco Total Care hospitals as 'located inside local Petco pet care centers,' operating under the visible Petco brand rather than a separately branded name that hides the parent company.

products.name: Chewy Vet Care
products.description: A small, newly launched chain of standalone general-practice clinics run by the publicly traded online retailer Chewy.

accessibility.note: AVMA's news coverage of Chewy's pending purchase of Modern Animal says Chewy 'currently owns 18 CVC practices across five states,' with the deal, if approved, expanding that to 47 locations.

ownership.note: The same AVMA article confirms Chewy is a public company, referencing its board-authorized share repurchase program and its investor relations disclosures; Chewy trades on the NYSE and reports quarterly results, unlike a privately held chain.

transparency.note: Chewy announced the clinics under its own name in a December 2023 investor relations press release, branding them 'Chewy Vet Care' rather than a name that obscures the parent company.

products.name: Dutch
products.description: A subscription video-call service that connects a pet owner with a licensed veterinarian for diagnosis, prescriptions, and advice, without a physical exam.

accessibility.note: Dutch's own site describes 10-minute video consultations with licensed veterinarians, covering 'over 150 issues' and handling 'over 90% of cases' virtually, plus at-home lab test kits and unlimited messaging for up to five pets under one membership; it cannot handle emergencies, wounds needing stitches, or anything requiring blood work, imaging, or surgery, for which it refers the owner to an in-person vet.

products.name: University veterinary teaching hospital
products.description: The teaching hospital run by an accredited veterinary college, usually taking referrals for specialty and complex cases alongside training students.

accessibility.note: AVMA's own list of accredited veterinary colleges names 30 fully accredited US veterinary colleges, plus 5 with provisional accreditation; each runs its own teaching hospital, so there are only a few dozen nationwide and most take specialty or referral cases rather than routine walk-in appointments.

ownership.note: Cornell's own site describes its Companion Animal Hospital as part of 'Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine,' seeing more than 39,000 patients a year and running a 24-hour emergency service alongside faculty-supervised referral care. A university teaching hospital like Cornell's answers to its public or nonprofit institution and its veterinary college's accreditation, not to a private investor or shareholders.

products.name: Independent, locally owned practice
products.description: A general practice owned by the veterinarian or veterinarians who work there, rather than by a national chain or an investment firm.

ownership.note: FTC Chair Lina Khan's June 2022 statement on a veterinary merger cites a 2021 trade-press estimate that 'frenetic merger activity among veterinary hospitals in 2021 has lifted the market share of corporate consolidators in the United States to close to 50% of all companion animal practice revenue,' meaning independent practices still accounted for roughly the other half; the same statement warns that private equity ownership in health care 'can incentivize practices that may reduce quality of care, increase costs for patients and payors.' An independent practice is owned directly by the treating veterinarian rather than a management company.

transparency.note: California's Veterinary Medical Board, a state regulator, requires every practice location to complete a 'Veterinary Premises Registration' and publishes disciplinary actions and citations against individual veterinarians and practices that the public can search directly; at an independent practice the registered premises and the treating veterinarian are the same person, so there is no separate corporate name standing between the two.

products.name: PetVet Care Centers
products.description: A general, specialty, emergency, and equine hospital chain that keeps each practice's local name and staff after buying it.

accessibility.note: PetVet's own site says it has 'more than 420 locally-led General Practice, Speciality, Emergency, and Equine hospitals' across the country; the page does not name an owner or investor.
